---
title: "07 — Q4: ITS1, ITS2 or full ITS"
author: "Adrien Taudière"
---

Does the ITSx region assigned change the accuracy, per method and database,
and what does it cost? Since OD 34 every dataset is assigned on its ITSx
inputs only; the datasets sequenced over the whole ITS are assigned three
times, on the ITS1, the ITS2 and the full ITS that ITSx extracts from the same
ASVs. This chapter compares those three regions on the two datasets that have
them and a truth: the **Tedersoo** Illumina mock and the **in silico** set.
Pauvert (ITS1 only), wood and air (one region, no truth) are not in it.
Figures: Q4.1 (per-rank × method), Q4.2 (per database), Q4.3 (cost beside
accuracy), Q4.4 (Tedersoo on the ASVs trimmed in every region); one tab per
dataset, ASVs, default settings.

**Read the in silico set apart.** Its reads were generated from records of
`Unite_s_all_20250219`, so on the three UNITE `_s_all` databases the exact
record of every ASV is in the reference (the positive control of
`in_silico_simulation.qmd`), and on the EUKARYOME ones it is not (OD 29a). The
region effect is read within a database, never across.

```{r setup}
here::i_am("analysis/07_q4_its_region.qmd")  # _quarto.yml would otherwise make here() root = analysis/
source(here::here("analysis/00_setup.R"))
region_order <- c("ITS1", "ITS2", "full")

# The scored columns of every dataset with more than one region: Tedersoo
# from chapter 01's cache, the in silico set from in_silico_simulation.qmd's
# (kept out of res_comp_tax, OD 29). ASVs, single methods, default settings.
res_tedersoo <- cache_read("res_comp_tax") |>
  group_by(dataset) |>
  filter(n_distinct(region) > 1) |>
  ungroup()
insilico_cache <- file.path(cache_dir, "res_insilico.rds")
res_insilico <- if (!analysis_mini && file.exists(insilico_cache)) {
  readRDS(insilico_cache) |> mutate(dataset = "insilico")
} else {
  NULL
}
res_q4 <- bind_rows(res_tedersoo, res_insilico) |>
  filter(unit == "ASV", !is_consensus) |>
  filter_default_settings() |>
  mutate(
    region = factor(region, levels = region_order),
    tax_level = factor(tax_level, levels = tax_order),
    view = factor(dataset, levels = unique(c(res_tedersoo$dataset, "insilico")))
  )
q4_datasets <- levels(droplevels(res_q4$view))

# The same scoring restricted to the real ASVs that ITSx trimmed in every
# region of the dataset (chapter 01, res_paired, Tedersoo only; unit
# "ASV_common", OD 38), and, for contrast, to every real ASV present in all
# the regions, trimmed or not ("ASV_common_all", the reading before OD 38).
res_paired_both <- cache_read("res_paired") |>
  filter(!is_consensus) |>
  filter_default_settings() |>
  mutate(
    region = factor(region, levels = region_order),
    tax_level = factor(tax_level, levels = tax_order),
    view = factor(dataset, levels = q4_datasets)
  )
res_paired <- filter(res_paired_both, unit == "ASV_common")
res_paired_all <- filter(res_paired_both, unit == "ASV_common_all")
n_common <- unique(res_paired$n_units_kept)
n_common_all <- unique(res_paired_all$n_units_kept)

# Real units trimmed by ITSx, and untrimmed (assigned on the whole amplicon),
# per region: the mocks from chapter 01, the in silico set from its stores.
itsx_trimming <- bind_rows(
  cache_read("itsx_trimming"),
  if ("insilico" %in% q4_datasets) {
    bind_rows(lapply(region_order, function(r) {
      is_trimmed <- itsx_trimmed(
        here("store_assign_taxo_insilico"),
        here("store_dada2_insilico"),
        r
      )
      tibble::tibble(
        dataset = "insilico",
        region = r,
        real_units = length(is_trimmed),
        trimmed = sum(is_trimmed),
        untrimmed = sum(!is_trimmed)
      )
    }))
  }
) |>
  filter(dataset %in% q4_datasets)

# The benchmark_costs of a dataset's assignment store (Tedersoo through
# costs_for(); the in silico store is not in analysis_datasets).
q4_costs <- function(dataset, res) {
  if (dataset == "insilico") {
    return(targets::tar_read(
      benchmark_costs,
      store = here("store_assign_taxo_insilico")
    ))
  }
  costs_for(dataset, res)
}
res_q4_cost <- lapply(q4_datasets, function(d) {
  rows <- filter(res_q4, dataset == d, metrics == "F1_score")
  rows |>
    left_join(
      q4_costs(d, rows) |> select(phase, wall_time_s),
      by = c("method_db" = "phase")
    )
}) |>
  bind_rows()

# One panel-tabset with a tab per dataset, in a chunk with results = "asis".
# As in view_tabs(), fun() must print() a figure before save_fig().
dataset_tabs <- function(fun) {
  cat("\n::: {.panel-tabset}\n\n")
  for (d in q4_datasets) {
    cat("### ", d, "\n\n", sep = "")
    fun(filter(res_q4, dataset == d), d)
    cat("\n\n")
  }
  cat(":::\n\n")
}
```

## Summary

```{r summary-data}
#| include: false
# Computed from the same rows as the tabs below (res_q4, default settings).
s07_by_region <- res_q4 |>
  filter(metrics == "F1_score", tax_level == "Genus") |>
  group_by(view, tax_level, algo, region) |>
  summarise(value = mean(values), .groups = "drop")
# Per dataset x rank x method: best minus worst region.
s07_spread <- s07_by_region |>
  group_by(view, tax_level, algo) |>
  summarise(spread = max(value) - min(value), .groups = "drop")
s07_best_region <- s07_by_region |>
  group_by(view, tax_level, region) |>
  summarise(value = mean(value), .groups = "drop")
s07_genus_best <- filter(s07_best_region, tax_level == "Genus")
s07_genus_spread <- filter(s07_spread, tax_level == "Genus")
s07_widest <- s07_genus_spread |>
  slice_max(spread, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
# blastn wall time, summed over the databases, full ITS against each region.
s07_blastn <- res_q4_cost |>
  filter(algo == "blastn", tax_level == "Genus", !is.na(wall_time_s)) |>
  distinct(view, region, db, wall_time_s) |>
  group_by(view, region) |>
  summarise(minutes = sum(wall_time_s) / 60, .groups = "drop")
s07_blastn_gain <- s07_blastn |>
  group_by(view) |>
  mutate(gain = minutes[region == "full"] / minutes) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(region != "full")
# The same reading on the ASVs trimmed in the three regions (Q4.4).
s07_paired_by_region <- res_paired |>
  filter(metrics == "F1_score", tax_level == "Genus") |>
  group_by(view, tax_level, algo, region) |>
  summarise(value = mean(values), .groups = "drop")
s07_paired_best <- s07_paired_by_region |>
  filter(tax_level == "Genus") |>
  group_by(view, region) |>
  summarise(value = mean(value), .groups = "drop")
s07_paired_spread <- s07_paired_by_region |>
  filter(tax_level == "Genus") |>
  group_by(view, algo) |>
  summarise(spread = max(value) - min(value), .groups = "drop")
# Words that follow the numbers, so that no adjective outlives the data.
s07_region_word <- if (max(s07_genus_spread$spread) < 0.03) {
  "below 0.03 for every method: at Genus the region barely matters"
} else {
  "0.03 or more for at least one method: the region matters there"
}
```

ASVs, default settings, F1 averaged over the nine reference databases; one
value per dataset (`r paste(q4_datasets, collapse = ", ")`).

- **Genus**: the best region is `r best_phrase(s07_genus_best, "region")`
  (mean over the four methods). Best minus worst region per method:
  `r fmt_range(s07_genus_spread$spread)`, `r s07_region_word`; the widest gap
  is `r s07_widest$algo` on `r s07_widest$view`
  (`r format(round(s07_widest$spread, 3), nsmall = 3)`).
- **Species** is no longer a primary endpoint here (OD 43): it is read by
  exact and near match in chapter 09; the `Gen_sp` rows below are secondary.
- **On the ASVs trimmed in all three regions** (Tedersoo, `r n_common` of
  the `r n_common_all` real ASVs common to the regions, Q4.4): the best
  region at Genus is `r best_phrase(s07_paired_best, "region")`; best minus
  worst region per method `r fmt_range(s07_paired_spread$spread)`.
- **blastn cost** (provisional, OD 31): the full ITS takes
  `r fmt_range(s07_blastn_gain$gain[s07_blastn_gain$region == "ITS1"], 1)`
  times the ITS1 time and
  `r fmt_range(s07_blastn_gain$gain[s07_blastn_gain$region == "ITS2"], 1)`
  times the ITS2 time, summed over the nine databases.

```{r summary-fig}
#| echo: false
fig_summary_07_f1_by_region <- s07_by_region |>
  ggplot(aes(x = region, y = value, colour = algo, group = algo)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~view, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "ITSx region", y = "Genus F1 (mean over databases)",
    colour = "Method"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
print(fig_summary_07_f1_by_region)
save_fig(fig_summary_07_f1_by_region, "fig_summary_07_f1_by_region", width = 9, height = 6)
```

The regions are cut from the same ASVs, but ITSx does not find every region in
every ASV. **An ASV whose region ITSx does not find stays in that region's
input with its whole sequence** (`keep_undetected = TRUE`, OD 38: no unit is
lost for Q1–Q3 and Q5), and the ASVs that become identical once trimmed are
merged. So the inputs of a region differ in two ways: they hold different
numbers of units, and some of their units are the untrimmed amplicon rather
than the region. On Tedersoo, whose reads carry 18S and 28S flanks around the
ITS, an untrimmed unit is one whose region ITSx did not detect. Q4.1–Q4.3
score every unit of each input; Q4.4 scores Tedersoo again on the ASVs ITSx
trimmed in all three regions.

**The in silico "full" input is not cut by ITSx, and need not be.** Its ASVs
come from UNITE records that UNITE has already cut to ITS1-5.8S-ITS2, so they
carry no SSU or LSU flank for ITSx to find: the uncut ASV is the full ITS.
Its ITS1 and ITS2 inputs are true ITSx regions.

```{r n-real}
#| echo: false
itsx_trimming |>
  mutate(region = factor(region, levels = region_order)) |>
  arrange(dataset, region) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c(
      "Dataset", "Region", "Real units", "Trimmed by ITSx",
      "Untrimmed (whole amplicon)"
    ),
    caption = "Real units of each region input: trimmed by ITSx, or kept on their whole sequence because ITSx did not find the region."
  )
```

## Q4.1 — Per-rank × method (F1, MCC)

Mean over the nine databases; bar = min–max over the databases.

```{r q4-1, results = "asis"}
dataset_tabs(function(res, d) {
  fig_q4_rank <- res |>
    filter(metrics %in% c("F1_score", "MCC")) |>
    group_by(metrics, tax_level, algo, region) |>
    summarise(
      value = mean(values),
      lo = min(values),
      hi = max(values),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = tax_level, y = value, colour = region, group = region)) +
    geom_linerange(
      aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
      position = position_dodge(width = 0.5),
      alpha = 0.5
    ) +
    geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.5), size = 2) +
    geom_line(position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
    facet_grid(metrics ~ algo) +
    labs(x = "Rank", y = "Value", colour = "ITSx region") +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), legend.position = "bottom")
  print(fig_q4_rank)
  save_fig(fig_q4_rank, paste0("fig_q4_rank_", d), width = 14, height = 7)
})
```

## Q4.2 — Per method × database (Genus, Gen_sp)

F1 of each region, one bar per database.

```{r q4-2, results = "asis"}
dataset_tabs(function(res, d) {
  fig_q4_db <- res |>
    filter(metrics == "F1_score", tax_level %in% c("Genus", "Gen_sp")) |>
    mutate(db = factor(db, levels = db_list)) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = db, y = values, fill = region)) +
    geom_col(position = position_dodge()) +
    facet_grid(tax_level ~ algo) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "F1", fill = "ITSx region") +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), legend.position = "bottom")
  print(fig_q4_db)
  save_fig(fig_q4_db, paste0("fig_q4_db_", d), width = 14, height = 7)
  # Genus F1 of each region minus the full ITS, per method x database.
  res |>
    filter(metrics == "F1_score", tax_level == "Genus") |>
    select(algo, db, region, values) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = region, values_from = values) |>
    mutate(
      `ITS1 − full` = round(ITS1 - full, 3),
      `ITS2 − full` = round(ITS2 - full, 3),
      across(c(ITS1, ITS2, full), \(x) round(x, 3))
    ) |>
    arrange(algo, factor(db, levels = db_list)) |>
    cat_kable(caption = "Genus F1 per region, and the difference to the full ITS.")
})
```

## Q4.3 — Cost beside accuracy

**Provisional costs** (OD 31): wall time of one computation (one method × one
database × one region), measured during the benchmark runs, not in the final
timing run (ROADMAP M2.4). blastn is the method whose cost depends on the
query: on wood, removing the conserved flanks with ITSx made it 13.4 times
faster (`HISTORY.md` §2, 2026-09-27); the full ITS keeps the 5.8S.

```{r q4-3, results = "asis"}
dataset_tabs(function(res, d) {
  rows <- filter(res_q4_cost, dataset == d, tax_level == "Genus", !is.na(wall_time_s))
  fig_q4_cost <- rows |>
    ggplot(aes(x = wall_time_s / 60, y = values, colour = region, shape = db)) +
    geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
    scale_x_log10() +
    scale_shape_manual(values = db_shapes) +
    facet_wrap(~algo, nrow = 1) +
    labs(
      x = "Wall time of the computation (min, log scale)",
      y = "Genus F1", colour = "ITSx region", shape = "Database"
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical")
  print(fig_q4_cost)
  save_fig(fig_q4_cost, paste0("fig_q4_cost_", d), width = 14, height = 6)
  # blastn per database: minutes per region, the full / region ratio and the
  # Genus F1 beside it.
  rows |>
    filter(algo == "blastn") |>
    distinct(db, region, wall_time_s, values) |>
    mutate(minutes = wall_time_s / 60, f1 = round(values, 3)) |>
    select(db, region, minutes, f1) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = region, values_from = c(minutes, f1)) |>
    # Ratios on the unrounded times: a rounded ITS1 time of 0.0 min gave Inf.
    mutate(
      `full / ITS1` = round(minutes_full / minutes_ITS1, 1),
      `full / ITS2` = round(minutes_full / minutes_ITS2, 1),
      across(starts_with("minutes_"), \(m) round(m, 1))
    ) |>
    arrange(factor(db, levels = db_list)) |>
    cat_kable(caption = "blastn: minutes per computation and Genus F1, per region.")
})
```

## Q4.4 — Tedersoo on the ASVs trimmed in every region

Each region scored again on the `r n_common` real ASVs that ITSx trimmed in
all three regions (chapter 01, `res_paired`, OD 38), each region keeping its
own controls. Solid: these ASVs; dotted: the `r n_common_all` ASVs present in
the three regions, trimmed or not (the untrimmed ones enter every region with
the same sequence and the same answers, so they dilute the differences);
dashed: every ASV of the region, as in Q4.1. A region effect that survives on
the trimmed ASVs is neither a change of unit set nor an untrimmed amplicon.

```{r q4-4}
#| fig-height: 6
s07_paired_all_by_region <- res_paired_all |>
  filter(metrics == "F1_score", tax_level %in% c("Genus", "Gen_sp")) |>
  group_by(view, tax_level, algo, region) |>
  summarise(value = mean(values), .groups = "drop")
q4_paired_lines <- bind_rows(
  s07_paired_by_region |> mutate(units = "trimmed in every region"),
  s07_paired_all_by_region |> mutate(units = "common, trimmed or not"),
  s07_by_region |>
    filter(view %in% unique(as.character(res_paired$view))) |>
    mutate(units = "every ASV of the region")
) |>
  mutate(
    units = factor(
      units,
      levels = c(
        "trimmed in every region",
        "common, trimmed or not",
        "every ASV of the region"
      )
    )
  )
fig_q4_paired <- q4_paired_lines |>
  ggplot(aes(x = region, y = value, colour = algo, linetype = units)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_line(aes(group = interaction(algo, units))) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("solid", "dotted", "dashed")) +
  facet_wrap(~tax_level, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "ITSx region", y = "F1 (mean over databases)", colour = "Method", linetype = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical")
print(fig_q4_paired)
save_fig(fig_q4_paired, "fig_q4_paired_tedersoo_illumina", width = 10, height = 6)
```

  mutate(
    `ITS1 − full` = round(ITS1 - full, 3),
    `ITS2 − full` = round(ITS2 - full, 3),
    across(c(ITS1, ITS2, full), \(x) round(x, 3))
  ) |>
  arrange(algo, factor(db, levels = db_list)) |>

```{r q4-4-dada2}
#| include: false
s07_dada2_paired <- s07_paired_by_region |>
  filter(tax_level == "Genus", algo == "dada2") |>
  arrange(desc(value))
```

For dada2 the three regions lie within
`r format(round(max(s07_dada2_paired$value) - min(s07_dada2_paired$value), 3), nsmall = 3)`
of each other (best: `r s07_dada2_paired$region[1]`), less than the spread of
its Genus F1 across seeds on Pauvert (up to 0.013, `HISTORY.md` §3d, OD 41):
no region is better than another for dada2. The result is the order of the
four methods together.
